name: IN JI
title: Backend Engineer

skill_groups.name: Infrastructure
items: AWS (EC2, ECS, RDS, S3, ECR, Route53, Lambda, SQS, Secrets Manager, CloudFront)

intro: **I enjoy simplifying repetitive work and improving the systems behind running services.** When building a feature, I consider how people will use it and what it will take to operate it day to day.

Seeing operations staff repeatedly rely on developers or connect to servers to complete routine tasks led me to build internal web tools they could use themselves. **Changing how work gets done through software** was rewarding, and it made me look for ways to remove manual work whenever I encountered it.

Expanding services across countries and migrating existing APIs taught me to look beyond the code being changed to the features and operations that depend on it. I am particularly interested in **making meaningful structural changes while keeping existing services running**.

With re:feel, an app I co-planned with a friend, I also built and operated a product myself. I developed the app and backend, handled deployment, and used usage data and feedback to refine its target audience and features after launch. I enjoy seeing how people use a product and turning their responses into the next improvement.

I now use MCP to bring product specifications and related code into context, and work with AI on implementation plans to speed up development. I review generated code myself and base architecture and technology decisions on the needs of the service and its operating environment.

companies.name: smaxh
companies.description: Tennis matching, lessons, and community platform. Backend development and operations for services in Korea, the US, and Australia.
highlights: **Python · Django · MySQL backend for match and lesson payments and settlement** — Built payment, cancellation, refund, and withdrawal flows. Supported a service whose monthly payment volume grew from **KRW 200M to 400M**, and transaction count from **16K to 30K**, between August and October 2025.

**Docker · Terraform · AWS integration of COOCON balance withdrawals** — Owned delivery from container, infrastructure, S3 configuration, and Secrets Manager setup to API development and deployment. Enabled SMAXH Pay withdrawals to bank accounts, with account registration, lookup, withdrawal, and transaction-history APIs.
**Django · MySQL development of no-show deposit payments, refunds, and settlement** — Contributed to the full deposit-processing flow; the deposit configuration rate was **78% in September 2026**.

**Django · OAuth expansion of app and web authentication** — Integrated Google, Apple, and Kakao web login with existing signup and account-linking flows. Separated app and web sessions and configured environment-specific deployment settings while preserving app compatibility.

**DynamoDB-based global account integration** — Kept country-specific databases separate while linking accounts through shared UUIDs. Added shared-state validation to login and token refresh to resolve cross-country inconsistencies in account closure and re-registration.

**Python · Django localization of matching services for the US and Australia** — Integrated local tennis-court data and processed match schedules in each court's time zone so services could operate on local time independently of server location.

**Django migration to shared APIs for social and tier-based matches** — Consolidated response and processing structures and reused payment and notification logic. Retained legacy endpoints so the existing app could coexist with the new APIs.

**pytest · Docker test environments and regression tests** — Used MySQL and DynamoDB Local to verify normal and failure paths for payments, refunds, settlement, authentication, and account linking. Wrote tests for duplicate processing and concurrent session refresh and revocation.

**Django · MySQL lesson development and query optimization** — Built recurring-schedule, application, payment, and settlement models and APIs. Used Datadog APM and SQL to diagnose bottlenecks and reduce repeated lookups, unnecessary joins, and aggregation work.

companies.name: Playtag
companies.description: AI video analysis of preschool children's behavior. Built internal web applications for analysis reruns and client configuration.
highlights: **Python web tool for rerunning failed video-analysis jobs** — Replaced manual server access and code execution with a web-based selection-and-submit workflow, reducing rerun preparation from **about 1 hour to 5 minutes or less**. Built and deployed the tool.

**Python web application for client configuration management** — Enabled operations staff to record and apply kindergarten schedules and settings directly, reducing developer handoffs and manual code changes. Deployed on a low-cost single instance suited to internal usage.
**Kotlin · Spring Boot APIs for kindergarten student management** — Built the complete set of new APIs **within a one-week sprint**, applying both technologies in production for the first time.

companies.name: Artue.io
companies.description: Art commerce and online exhibition platform. Worked on media processing, AWS infrastructure, and API migration for a running service.
highlights: **Python · Serverless Framework · S3/Lambda asynchronous media processing** — Generated display-specific WebP images and multiple video resolutions after upload. Used in-memory streams and filtered derived-file events to eliminate temporary-file handling and duplicate conversions.

**Terraform · AWS EC2/ECS infrastructure and Auto Scaling configuration** — Changed instances from **t3.medium to t3.small** and the CPU scaling target from **40% to 20%**, consolidating environment-specific capacity settings.

**NestJS · TypeORM migration of running APIs** — Migrated customer, artwork, and purchasing functionality while **running v2 and v3 APIs in parallel**. Added tests and supported feature-by-feature frontend adoption to limit the impact of the changes.

**NestJS · TypeORM multi-currency purchasing and payments** — Applied exchange rates, discounts, and shipping costs across carts, orders, and payments for currencies including EUR and THB. Integrated Naver Pay, supported its approval process, and restored coupons on cancellation.

companies.name: Viewee Inc.
companies.description: Services connecting user-contributed data, AI analysis, and blockchain rewards. Developed data validation automation and transaction APIs.
highlights: **Python · Airflow automation of image-annotation review** — Applied bounding-box and OCR cross-checks and text-similarity validation to labels previously reviewed by hand, and automated recurring checks.
**TypeScript · NestJS APIs for EarnTube token transactions** — Built history models to track transaction results and hashes, and migrated legacy points history.

companies.name: re:feel
companies.description: AI journaling app offering diary analysis and illustrations. Co-planned with a friend; personally developed and deployed the app and backend.
highlights: **Django/DRF · MySQL · React/Capacitor development and launch of an AI journaling app** — Co-planned the product with a friend, personally developed the app and backend, and handled AWS deployment, **launching on iOS and Android in about two months**.

**Gemini · Django/DRF integration of AI analysis and in-app purchases** — Connected asynchronous analysis and illustration results, translation, server-side purchase validation, and access entitlements to the app experience.

**Firebase data and user feedback for product improvements** — Shifted focus to Korean users and combined feature improvements with social media promotion; **cumulative signups grew from about 10 to over 100 within weeks**.
